# Introduction {.unnumbered}

This online book contains materials for a work-in-progress course on the
fundamentals of data science abd computational population genomics and
inference, with a strong focus on building a solid foundation for modern
reproducible research and computer programming in R.

The general structure of the final book (to be developed over the course of
2025-2026) will take the form of a series of chapters serving as worksheets of
exercises on various interlinked topics from computer programming, data science,
and computational population genomics. The primary goal is for students to walk
through these worksheets in a classroom under the guidance of a lecturer, but
each chapter is also suitable for self-study---to serve as a handy reference of
"reciples" and example pipelines, and tutorial for daily research work.

The main intended audience are relatively novice researchers who have just
started (or are about to start) their careers in computational population
genomics and evolutionary genomics, such as master students or doctoral
students. However, these materials have also been used in workshops attended by
researchers with significant experience in population genomics, who felt they
lack the confidence in modern practices in reproducible computational data
science or had not had the opportunity to engage with fundamental concepts in
population genomics in a simulation-based, exploratory manner such as is offered
by this book course.
